question.text: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The velocity of water is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>V</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is _________.

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the change in pressure can be written as

P1-P2=12ρv2   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

4.5×104-2.0×104=12×103×v2⇒2.5×104=12×103×v2⇒v2=50⇒v=50

Hence, V=50.
